The diagram covers the two modules and the data file:
- **`src/app.py`:** `place_order` checks stock, calls `total`, decrements stock, then builds the order.
- **`src/payments.py`:** `charge` returns `{ok, id}` and never raises. In the current code it fails only when the card token is missing.
- **`data/orders.json`:** `place_order` reads the existing orders and writes the new one back.

# shopfront

A tiny order service used as the fixture for Junior-dev's headless runs. Customers place
orders through `POST /orders`; the service checks stock, charges the card through the
payment provider, and records the order. Orders are kept in `data/orders.json`.

Run it with `python -m src.app`. It needs no database. You will recieve an email receipt
when an order is placed.

# Architecture Components and the path an order takes, as implemented in `src/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD Caller["Caller
(calls place_order)"] subgraph App["src/app.py"] Place["place_order(customer, items, card_token)"] Stock{"STOCK has enough
of every item?"} Total["total(items)
using PRICES"] Decrement["Decrement STOCK"] Record["Build order
id = len(orders) + 1"] end subgraph Pay["src/payments.py"] Charge["charge(card_token, amount_cents)
returns {ok, id}"] TokenOk{"card_token
present?"} end Store[("data/orders.json")] Caller --> Place Place --> Stock Stock -- no --> RejStock["Return rejected:
out of stock"] Stock -- yes --> Total Total --> Charge Charge --> TokenOk TokenOk -- no --> RejPay["Return rejected:
payment failed"] TokenOk -- yes --> Decrement Decrement --> Record Record <-- "read existing, write back" --> Store Record --> Placed["Return placed + order"] ``` ## Order lifecycle 1. `place_order` checks every requested item against the in-memory `STOCK`. Any shortfall returns `rejected` ("out of stock") and nothing else happens. 2. `total` prices the order from `PRICES` (in cents). 3. `charge` is called with the card token and total. It returns `{ok, id}` and never raises. In the current code a missing token fails and any other token succeeds. 4. On success, stock is decremented, the order is appended to `data/orders.json` with the payment id, and `placed` is returned. ## Notes - `STOCK` is in memory only, so it resets on restart. `orders.json` is the only persisted state. - `README.md` describes a `POST /orders` endpoint and an emailed receipt. Neither exists in `src/`: `app.py` has no HTTP layer and no email code, so they are left out of the diagram.
